memories.content: Use a flow diagram rather than a sequence table when alternate procedural branches lead to different outcomes.
Draw alternate branches and their resulting outcomes in the same flow diagram so readers can compare them at once.
The visual fidelity of a prototype may differ from its functional fidelity.
A flow diagram can make alternate branches and their different outcomes visible in one view.
HCI reviewers often skim prototype screens and interaction flow diagrams before reading the main text.
Readers can understand the overall branching shape of a procedure more quickly from a flow diagram than from rows read one at a time.
Redrawing a branching flow diagram after a procedural change usually takes longer than updating one row in a table.
Reviewers often inspect the proposal’s main visual before reading the procedural explanation in full.
Specify in one sentence the user population and actual usage environment to which the design knowledge applies.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through the specified target population and environment.
Specify the workflow, technical infrastructure, and operational-authority conditions that must match before applying the design guidelines at another field site.
The transferability of field design knowledge depends not only on user characteristics but also on workflow and technological–organizational infrastructure.
The user tends to apply results confirmed at one deployment site to all similar organizations.

analysis.overview: The reference frame concentrates on choosing and maintaining flow diagrams for branching procedures, distinguishing prototype fidelities, and anticipating visual-first review. The compared frame concentrates on defining transferability boundaries for field design knowledge and recognizing a tendency to overgeneralize site-specific results. No substantive cross-frame overlap or contradiction is present.

relations.reason: These memories split one reference-only design claim across format choice, diagram composition, simultaneous visibility, and faster comprehension.
relations.summary: Flow diagrams should show alternate procedural branches and outcomes together when they communicate branching structure more effectively than sequential table rows.

relations.reason: This independently useful distinction appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: A prototype’s visual fidelity and functional fidelity may differ.

relations.reason: The reference memories restate one visual-first review behavior at different levels of specificity.
relations.summary: Reviewers often inspect prototype or proposal visuals and interaction-flow material before reading the full explanation.

relations.summary: The applicability boundary of field design knowledge should be specified and judged using population, environment, workflow, technical infrastructure, and organizational-authority conditions.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only guidance defines field-knowledge applicability through population, environment, workflow, infrastructure, and authority conditions, while noting a tendency to generalize one site’s results too broadly.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only guidance favors unified flow diagrams for branching procedures, notes their comprehension and maintenance tradeoffs, distinguishes visual from functional prototype fidelity, and describes reviewers’ tendency to inspect visuals first.
